text: ← RETURN TO SELECTED WORK CASE STUDY 03 · APPLIED AI ARCHITECTURE LESSONS-LEARNED MEMORY BM25 SEARCH ZERO-DEPENDENCY PYTHON Cognitive Memory Core — A Lessons-Learned Memory for AI Coding Assistants AI coding assistants forget your corrections when the session ends. Memory Core saves each mistake as a lesson, finds the matching lessons before the next task starts, and turns lessons that keep coming back into written rules. It is pure Python with no dependencies. PROBLEM Coding agents forget corrections between sessions and repeat the same mistakes. CONSTRAINT Recall runs before every task on a local workstation, so it uses the Python standard library only: no model download, no vector database. DECISION Field-weighted BM25 with tag and severity boosts over a JSONL store of post-mortems. MEASURED RESULT On 30 held-out queries: recall@3 0.90, MRR 0.87, 0.81 ms p50 on the 10-entry store (i5-12400F, Python 3.11, 2026-10-02). A naive substring baseline scores about the same at this size (eval). CODE cognitive-memory-core/eval, rerun with python eval/run_eval.py ⚡ Launch Live Memory Simulator ↓ Architecture Deep Dive ↓ View Code on GitHub ↗ PLATFORM Antigravity Rules · Discord Multi-Agent System · Local CLI DISCIPLINE Search & Developer Tooling ROLE Developer & Systems Builder (Solo) STACK Python 3.11 (Stdlib) · BM25 Scorer · JSONL ● THE ENGINEERING CHALLENGE (SESSION AMNESIA) AI coding assistants start every session blank, so they repeat mistakes you already corrected. The usual fix, a vector database, adds a model download and a stack of dependencies. ● THE ARCHITECTURE SOLUTION (BM25 LESSON SEARCH) Built a lessons-learned memory in the Python standard library only. Lessons live in a JSONL file, BM25 keyword search finds the relevant ones before each task, and repeated lessons are compiled into a rules file the assistant reads. 0 Dependencies PYTHON STANDARD LIBRARY ONLY BM25 Scored KEYWORD SEARCH OVER PAST LESSONS 10 Rules COMPILED FROM REPEATED LESSONS CI-Tested PYTEST ON EVERY PUSH Show the lesson recall loop TABLE OF CONTENTS 01. Session Amnesia Dilemma 02. Design Decisions 03. What Broke & What I’d Change 04. Live Recall Simulator 05. The 4 Parts of Memory Core 06. How BM25 Ranks Lessons 07. The 10 Lessons in the Store 08. Impact & Benchmarks // 01 · CONTEXT & MOTIVATION The Dilemma: AI Session Amnesia Contemporary AI coding assistants are fundamentally stateless between sessions. Every new conversation, branch switch, or tool invocation begins with a clean slate. This creates a frustrating, repetitive developer experience: Regression Loops: An agent repeats known anti-patterns (e.g. nested PowerShell quotes, robotic copy on lifestyle brands, or Netlify subdirectory 404 order). Tacit Knowledge Loss: Non-obvious nuances uncovered through painful debugging are lost the moment the chat window closes. Context Window Bloat: Shoving entire multi-thousand-line project histories into prompt headers wastes token bandwidth and degrades attention quality. The goal is simple: a correction made once is remembered next time, without pasting the whole project history into every prompt. // 02 · DESIGN DECISIONS Design Decisions & Their Costs Each card is one decision: what I chose, what I passed over, why, and what it costs. The evidence links point at the public code or result file at a pinned commit. ADR-MEM-01 Keyword BM25 in the standard library, not a vector database Decision Field-weighted BM25 over the JSONL lesson store, with tag and severity boosts, in the Python standard library only. Alternatives Dense embeddings with ChromaDB, FAISS or sqlite-vss. Why No model download, no embedding step on every write, and exact identifiers such as TerminatorExpectedAtEndOfString match as single tokens. 0.81 ms p50 on the real 10-entry store (500 calls, 2026-10-02). Cost It misses paraphrases that share no words with the rule (3 of 30 held-out queries) and is not clearly better than a substring baseline at this size. Latency grows linearly: 67 ms p50 at 1,000 entries and 695 ms at 10,000 (synthetic stores). Evidence eval/results/2026-10-02.md · recall.py ADR-MEM-02 An OS file lock around every write, then an atomic replace Decision reflect.py holds an OS lock (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl elsewhere) on store.jsonl.lock for the whole read-modify-write, writes a uniquely named temp file, and swaps it in with os.replace. Alternatives Append to the JSONL file without a lock, or an age-based lockfile that other writers can take over. Why Without the lock, two writers both read N lessons and both write N+1, so one lesson is lost. The OS releases the lock if its holder dies, so there is never a stale lock to reclaim. Cost Other writers poll every 20 ms and give up with TimeoutError after 10 s. On Windows the swap fails while a reader has the store open, so it is retried for up to 1 s. The .lock file must stay on disk. Evidence reflect.py · test_reflect_safety.py // 03 · RETROSPECTIVE What Broke & What I Would Change ⚠️ What Broke in V1 Unmeasured retrospective, recalled rather than logged: naive substring matching seemed to fire on generic coding words like error, file, and test, injecting unrelated rules into the prompt context. The held-out eval (Evals & Metrics, below) measures recall, not false positives, so it neither confirms nor rules this out. ✓ The Engineering Fix Implemented tokenization with an English coding stopword filter, added 3.0× weighting to exact domain tags, and introduced severity multipliers (1.4× for critical bugs) to isolate true matches. // 04 · REAL-TIME RECALL DEMO Interactive Demo: Find Lessons Before a Task Search the real lesson store below. Type a task or a bug, and BM25 ranks the 10 lessons by how well their symptoms, causes and rules match your words: LIVE LESSON SEARCH EXPERIENCE_STORE.JSONL · 10 LESSONS CLIENT-SIDE BM25 · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER Find Lessons ⚡ SUGGESTIONS: ☕ Coffee Copy 📐 Flexbox Brackets 🌐 Netlify 404 🇵🇭 PH Payments 💻 PowerShell Quotes 🐍 Windows CP1252 🚀 Git Deploy 📄 Doc Parsing 🔄 API Backoff 📊 Quantifiable Metrics ## ⚡ MATCHING LESSONS (checked before the task) Matched 2 lesson(s) for query: "navigation flexbox alignment wide screen" ### [MEM-002] CSS-LAYOUT (Relevance Score: 16.50) • MANDATORY RULE: Never insert spaced bracket text '[ LABEL ]' in navigation or inline-flex elements. If bracket styling is desired, use CSS ::before and ::after pseudo-elements, or guarantee no whitespace before the bracket and enforce 'white-space: nowrap;' on the parent element. • AVOIDED SYMPTOM: Trailing closing bracket ']' wrapped onto a separate line underneath the link label on wide screens • KEYWORDS: css, flexbox, navigation, whitespace, typography, layout, responsive, ui ### [MEM-010] RESUME-WRITING (Relevance Score: 2.75) • MANDATORY RULE: Always include quantifiable percentages, latency benchmarks, or dollar amounts in resume bullet points. • AVOIDED SYMPTOM: Vague, subjective resume bullet points failing ATS semantic parsers and technical hiring manager screens • KEYWORDS: resume, ats, career, metrics, quantifiable, writing, benchmarks, numbers // 05 · ENGINE SPECIFICATION The 4 Parts of Memory Core No vector database and no pip packages. It needs only standard Python 3: 📂 PILLAR 01 · DATA LEDGER Lesson Store An append-only JSONL file. Each lesson records what triggered the mistake, the symptom, the root cause, the rule to follow, tags, severity, and how often it has happened. experience_store.jsonl ⚡ PILLAR 02 · RETRIEVAL Lesson Search BM25 keyword search across past lessons, with extra weight for matching tags and for lessons that keep recurring. Returns the top matches fast enough to run before every task (measured latency and its conditions are under Results). recall.py · BM25 Algo 🔄 PILLAR 03 · REFLECTION Lesson Logger A CLI and Python API to record a new lesson. A near-duplicate in the same domain is merged into its closest match by word overlap (Jaccard), so a repeated mistake strengthens the existing lesson instead of adding a copy. --supersedes MEM-xxx retires an outdated rule: recall, dedupe and crystallize skip it from then on. reflect.py · Auto-Dedupe 💎 PILLAR 04 · COMPILER Rule Compiler Groups lessons by topic and compiles them into a rules file (learned_rules.md) that the coding assistant reads at the start of every session. crystallize.py → learned_rules.md // 06 · ALGORITHMIC MECHANICS How BM25 Ranks Lessons Vector embeddings alone frequently struggle with precise syntactic rules (e.g. distinguishing `"` from `'` in PowerShell or exact CSS properties like white-space: nowrap). I designed a domain-weighted BM25 scoring algorithm: Score(D, Q) = ∑ IDF(qᵢ) · [ (TF_weighted · (k₁ + 1)) / (TF_weighted + k₁ · (1 - b + b · (|D| / avgDL))) ] · SeverityMult · FreqMult Key architectural nuances: Multi-Field Weighting: Tags are weighted at 3.0×, triggers at 2.5×, and symptoms at 2.0× relative to generic code diffs. Frequency Compounding: Lessons encountered multiple times receive an automatic multiplier (1.0 + min(0.5, (freq - 1) * 0.1)), ensuring battle-tested rules rank highest. Zero Dependencies: No PyTorch, no HuggingFace, no ChromaDB. Pure Python standard library ensures instant execution across any terminal or CI/CD container. // 07 · ACTIVE PRODUCTION KNOWLEDGE The 10 Lessons in the Store The store holds 10 lessons, each from a real mistake in my own projects: ID DOMAIN OBSERVED SYMPTOM RULE MEM-001 Copywriting Robotic terms (SPECIMEN, PROTOCOL) in food e-commerce Strictly forbid sci-fi jargon for culinary/hospitality; use grounded tactile terms (Fresh Roast, Curated, Warm Batch, Shopping Bag). MEM-002 CSS Layout Closing bracket ']' wrapped onto separate line on desktop Never insert loose spaced bracket text inside inline-flex navigation elements; enforce white-space: nowrap;. MEM-003 Edge Routing Netlify subdirectory /aura-store loads 404 page Explicit subfolder rewrite rules MUST precede the global catch-all rule (/* /404.html 404) in both _redirects and netlify.toml. MEM-004 Localization US card-only checkout fails Philippine conversion Philippine e-commerce must feature GCash, Maya, QR Ph, and Cash on Delivery (COD) alongside domestic +63 phone formatting. MEM-005 CLI / Shell PowerShell TerminatorExpectedAtEndOfString crash Never nest unescaped double quotes inside double-quoted PowerShell commands; use single quotes or direct script invocations. MEM-006 Windows Python UnicodeEncodeError on terminal stdout Reconfigure stdout with sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8') or use ASCII status tokens to avoid cp1252 charmap crashes. MEM-007 Deployment Manual Netlify direct uploads causing untracked git drift Always deploy web apps by committing and pushing to GitHub; Netlify listens to the repository and deploys pinned commit states. MEM-008 Doc Parsing Cover letter body prematurely truncated on portfolio URL lines Never terminate cover letter parsing on contact lines containing portfolio links; only terminate on major structural markdown headers. MEM-009 API Resiliency HTTP 429 Too Many Requests rate limits crashing async Discord loops Always implement exponential backoff retry (sleep 2–4s) and a multi-model rotation pool on both Groq and Gemini. MEM-010 Resume Writing Subjective responsibility bullets failing ATS semantic parsers Every résumé experience bullet MUST lead with active verbs and quantify impact with verified metrics, latencies, or percentages. // 08 · EVALS & METRICS Retrieval Evals & Benchmarks pytest Automated Tests Recall, dedup, write safety & redaction, run by GitHub Actions on every push 0 External Packages Zero pip packages / pure stdlib 0.90 Recall@3, Held-Out Queries 30 paraphrased queries · MRR 0.87 Retrieval Eval: BM25 vs a Naive Substring Baseline Each of the 30 queries is a paraphrase labelled with the one rule it should retrieve, and a test fails if any query copies a 4-word run from the store. I wrote 15; the other 15 are with an independent reviewer to replace or approve, so I'm not only grading my own test. The baseline ranks rules by how many query words appear in them as substrings. Retriever recall@1 recall@3 MRR BM25 (recall.py) 0.83 0.90 0.87 Naive substring baseline 0.80 0.93 0.87 Store size Calls p50 p95 10 entries (real store) 500 0.81 ms 0.87 ms 1,000 entries (synthetic) 100 67 ms 70 ms 10,000 entries (synthetic) 20 695 ms 744 ms Measured 2026-10-02 with eval/run_eval.py on an Intel Core i5-12400F, Windows 11, Python 3.11.9, commit a9a7e96 of cognitive-memory-core. Each call includes reading and parsing the JSONL store. Synthetic stores are the real entries plus seeded filler drawn from the store's vocabulary. Full output: eval/results/2026-10-02.md. What this shows: on today's 10-entry store, BM25 is not clearly better than a substring search. It ties on MRR, and with 10 entries a top-3 list covers 30% of the store, so recall@3 says little. Its three misses are paraphrases with no shared words, such as "add numbers to the achievements in my CV" for the résumé-metrics rule, which no keyword method can catch. Latency grows linearly with the store, because every call re-reads and re-scores it. CI now fails if BM25 recall@3 or MRR falls below these numbers minus a tolerance. ← PREVIOUS CASE STUDY 02 · Manas: Ciel (Voice AI Copilot & HUD) NEXT CASE STUDY → 04 · Aura Coffee & Kitchen (Specialty Commerce)
